name: postpartum care overview
title: A postpartum problem sorted into mood (blues, depression, psychosis, told apart by how long and how severe, with the PHQ-2 and EPDS screen and its cut-offs) or fever and bleeding after the first 24 hours (delayed postpartum hemorrhage, puerperal infection), each with presentation, assessment and treatment in order; panels on the normal return to baseline and on clots, discharge and the perineum

root.title: After the birth: the normal return to baseline, or a complication?
lines: the complication is whatever breaks the timetable: blues past 2 weeks · bright red bleeding back after 24 h · fever on 2 of the first 10 days

groups.title: MOOD: how LONG, how SEVERE, is she in touch with reality?
BLEEDING or FEVER after the first 24 hours
lines: bleeding in the first 24 h: see the POSTPARTUM HEMORRHAGE chart

head: h
Postpartum depression
major depression within 6 months of delivery
clue: Blues > 2 weeks, or SEVERE in the first 2
• low mood, anhedonia, guilt, sleep, energy, appetite
• severe: poor bonding, suicidal or homicidal ideas
inv: at ANY total → immediate mental health assessment

head: h
Postpartum psychosis
rare, often with another mood disorder
h
Delayed postpartum hemorrhage
bleeding ↑ MORE than 24 h after birth
h
Puerperal infection
temperature > 38.0 °C on any 2 of the first 10 days, NOT counting the first 24 h
inv: also long labour or rupture of membranes, manual placenta removal
Clostridium sordellii or perfringens, toxic shock syndrome

panels.title: Back to baseline: the normal timetable
items: lochia for up to 56 days (rubra → serosa → alba) · uterus back to non-pregnant size by 4 weeks
ovulation can come BEFORE the first period: lactational amenorrhea is NOT contraception · not breastfeeding: ovulation and menses at ~6–8 weeks
contraception from 6 weeks · NO estrogen before 21 days (clot risk)
pelvic floor physiotherapy for EVERY patient, from 6 weeks

panels.title: Clots, sleep and going home
items: venous thromboembolism: greatest risk POSTPARTUM (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis) → low-molecular-weight heparin
insomnia: sleep hygiene first · cognitive behavioural therapy if persistent · rule out a mood disorder
home before 48 h: check bleeding, bowel, bladder, baby care · NOT with preeclampsia, postpartum hemorrhage, fever or an unstable condition
perineum: clean, dry, sitz baths · NO rectal medicines after a 3rd or 4th degree tear
